label: Run 2 · all 8 chats
note: Every chat of run 2 (the writer is the author and the authority): the same pair, the same brief and the same prompt, each written by a different writer.

chat.variety.why: All eight chats run nearly the same night. Each opens with Reuben's flourish plus an alibi for replying fast (kettle, cab, rain). Brick answers "hm." and a numbered anatomical disclosure, someone pastes a note by accident and says "ignore that," a confession cascade follows (ring-light shadow, eleven seconds and "we can just watch something," Delphine's one plain sentence, the cropped portrait nobody paid twelve pounds/quid to fix, the dropped work invite, the self-built clone that unmatched him). The finale is nearly always the clipboard handover, a minute-by-minute sex agenda, present-tense narration "so I know I'm in the room," and a hand flat on the back with talk of lentils or landlords. Whole sentences recur in far more than two chats, so this is well below the line. It stays above 1 because some things do shift between chats: who leaks the note (Reuben in David, Armstrong/Bain, Leonard and Waller-Bridge; Brick in Coel, Saunders, Parker and Pinter), the date (tonight, Thursday or Friday), and the coda (Armstrong/Bain's eleven-second silence, Saunders's "Stephen sounds like a prick," Coel's tile spacer).
evidence: Very few, very right things. (Coel; near-identical in Armstrong/Bain, Saunders, Waller-Bridge)
watched her face shut like a shopfront (Coel; also Leonard, Waller-Bridge, Pinter)

chat.variety.raise: Give each writer a different spine, with different wounds surfacing and no shared clipboard-agenda finale, so that no beat sequence or stock line appears in more than half the chats.
